request: leadCapture duplicate policy -- what happens when the same normalized email submits more than once?
rationale: A lead with the same normalized email must be rejected rather than silently accepted as a duplicate.
evidence: tests/prd_leadCapture.json description: duplicate handling raised as an explicit open design question.
Experiments 1/2: Database Agent independently invented a real duplicate policy (unique index or GROUP BY/HAVING check) every time, unprompted.
Experiments 1/2: Backend never inspected the SP embedded error field -- leadCaptures_sp always returns HTTP 200 regardless.
Experiments 1/2: Frontend only checks res.ok -- a duplicate rejection (200 + embedded error) reads as success.

database: Normalize email (lower/trim) before storage or comparison.
Enforce rejection via a persistent UNIQUE constraint, not only application-logic GROUP BY/HAVING.
backend: The create/upsert wrapper must inspect the SP's embedded result.error field and return a non-2xx status for a duplicate rejection.
Never pass through the SP raw 200 response unconditionally when the embedded result indicates an error.
frontend: Treat a response with an embedded error or duplicate indication as a failure even when HTTP status is 200.
res.ok alone must not be the only failure signal for this module's create call.
